title: Listening on: http://localhost:8080 by default when a mutable jar is deployed to OpenShift
body:
**Describe the bug**
(Describe the problem clearly and concisely.)
When a mutable jar is deployed to OpenShift via a binary build, localhost:8080 is listening by default than 0.0.0.0:8080 so the endpoint(i.e. REST API) can't be accessed externally via a router.

**Expected behavior**
(Describe the expected behavior clearly and concisely.)
Listening on: http://0.0.0.0:8080

**Actual behavior**
(Describe the actual behavior clearly and concisely.)
Listening on: http://localhost:8080

**To Reproduce**

Link to a small reproducer (preferably a Maven project if the issue is not Gradle-specific).

Or attach an archive containing the reproducer to the issue.

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Add the below package type(quarkus.package.type=mutable-jar)
2. oc new-build registry.access.redhat.com/ubi8/openjdk-11:1.3 --binary --name=quarkus-remote -l app=quarkus-remote
3. rm -rf target/binary && mkdir -p target/binary && cp -r target/remote-dev-demo-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT-runner.jar target/lib target/binary
4. oc start-build quarkus-remote --from-dir=target/binary
5. oc new-app quarkus-remote -e QUARKUS_LAUNCH_DEVMODE=true
6. oc expose service quarkus-remote
7. See the pod logs then access the route URL

**Configuration**
```properties
# Add your application.properties here, if applicable.
quarkus.package.type=mutable-jar
```

**Screenshots**
(If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your problem.)
